title: Sahara India Real Estate Corp. Ltd. & Ors. v. SEBI
crime_type: Unlawful Public Deposit Mobilization / Ponzi Mechanics / Contempt of Court
source: Supreme Court of India Judgment & Indian Kanoon (doc/1359141)
location: Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh & New Delhi, India
evidence: Mobilization of over ₹24,000 crore from 30 million small retail rural investors through Optionally Fully Convertible Debentures (OFCD)
Failure to maintain genuine investor identity records or KYC dossiers during massive cash collection drives
Submission of truckloads of unverifiable and illegible paper application forms to SEBI headquarters
Supreme Court findings of deliberate obfuscation of public issue rules
modus_operandi: Issued Optionally Fully Convertible Debentures (OFCDs) to tens of millions of rural and semi-urban small depositors while falsely styling the issue as a private placement to evade statutory SEBI public prospectus compliance. Used a nationwide network of collection agents collecting cash without proper banking KYC.
personality_disorder: Cult-like corporate autocracy, paternalistic grandeur, and defiant resistance to regulatory authority.
common_traits: Circumventing public issue compliance under private placement guises
Deliberate document flooding to exhaust regulatory capacity
summary: Historic Supreme Court judgment holding that any security issue offered to more than 49 individuals constitutes a public offer subject to SEBI jurisdiction. The Supreme Court ordered refund of ₹24,000+ crore and imprisoned promoter Subrata Roy for non-compliance.
